extracted.intended_audience: R package authors, volunteer reviewers, and the rOpenSci / scientific software community
extracted.subtask_description: Peer code-review process for R packages submitted to rOpenSci: editors check fit, reviewers evaluate usability/quality/style, and authors address recommendations via a public GitHub-issue workflow to gain an rOpenSci stamp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit to rOpenSci (scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an author submits a package, our editors evaluate it for fit according to our criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some submissions are turned away prior to review when out-of-scope (the post notes only 1 rejection for lack of fit in the pilot). Fit is a gating criterion before assigning reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usability
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate the package for usability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usability is evaluated alongside quality and style based on rOpenSci guidelines; reviewers are expected to give concrete feedback in the public GitHub issue and may suggest improvements or demonstrate problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate the package for overall software quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality evaluation goes beyond CRAN automated checks (which primarily ensure installability). Reviewers assess code correctness, tests, robustness, and other quality aspects per the guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate coding style and project style conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style assessment is part of the review suite (documentation style, API consistency, idiomatic R usage). Reviewers may point to 'the right way to do [X]' and teach best practices via the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public GitHub-issue workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: The review process is conducted entirely through the GitHub issue system: authors submit by opening an issue and reviewers post reviews as comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The entire process is open and public from the start; reviewers and authors are known to each other and can communicate directly. Reviewers may @tag others for outside expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of pull requests for contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers can contribute directly to the package via pull requests when that is more efficient than describing changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using PRs leverages GitHub in-line commenting and can speed up implementing fixes. The post suggests possibly requiring PR-style submissions to better use these features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-adversarial review tone
rubrics_metrics.description: A design goal is to keep reviews non-adversarial — focusing on improving software quality rather than judging the package or authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Openness of the process and a code of conduct are cited as incentives for courteous, constructive reviews; reviewers are expected to behave accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance condition: author implements recommended changes
rubrics_metrics.description: After reviewers evaluate and the author makes recommended changes, the package gets the rOpenSci stamp in its README and is added to the collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Packages requiring significant revisions can remain on hold until authors incorporate changes and update the discussion thread; because packages are already public and open-source, there is no time-to-publication pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: No explicit rejecting (except out-of-scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: rOpenSci does not explicitly reject packages, except turning some away prior to review when they are out-of-scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy stems from the fact submitted packages are public/open-source; packages needing major work can stay on hold rather than being formally rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer time expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical review effort reported by reviewers ranged from 1–10 hours, with an average of about 4 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This time does not include further correspondence or re-review. The post highlights reviewer time as a sustainability concern and that the process currently feels like voluntary community service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of process start and end
rubrics_metrics.description: The process should clearly explain how to get started and how the review is supposed to wrap up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors updated a reviewer guide and added links to previous reviews. The post recommends clearer communication and possibly enforcing deadlines for authors to respond so reviewers know when to consider a review finished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote best practices (CI, documentation, testing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A key outcome of review is teaching and encouraging best practices such as continuous integration, good documentation, and tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many reviewers and reviewees reported learning about and valuing CI and other practices; reviewers are expected to recommend these improvements as part of quality/style feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automation and tooling to reduce burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Automate parts of the review process and add tooling to increase value for reviewer/reviewee time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions include submitting packages as pull requests to leverage inline commenting, moving CI/test setup from authors to an rOpenSci pipeline, adding rOpenSci-specific tests, and using automated reminders to keep reviews moving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaling & reviewer incentives (editor handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: To scale, expand the reviewer pool and use multiple handling editors to assign and track reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post notes the need to maintain reviewer enthusiasm and avoid overburdening reviewers; bringing in more reviewers via networks and multiple handling editors is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility/credit incentives for authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors value feedback more than the badge, but additional incentives (visibility/credit) could encourage more submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible incentives include badges (e.g., from Center for Open Science), easier routes to publishing software papers, or other mechanisms to increase recognition after passing review.
